GruntWorx should inherit Instead’s operational safeguards, with vendor-specific limits and mappings verified against GruntWorx’s API.

1. **Rate limits must reflect the vendor’s actual accounting.** Instead has per-connection, per-API-group budgets plus an app-wide ceiling. Defaults include **5 docs requests/minute**, **50 entities/minute**, and **500 app requests/minute**; production defaults to **3,000 app requests/minute**. The group check runs first so a rejected job does not consume the app budget. Unknown groups fall into a budgeted `default` bucket. Preserve that discipline and `Retry-After` handling, but configure GruntWorx’s own scopes and numbers. Ordinary operations allow 10 retries; throttling reschedules work with its retry count reset, so this is **not a wall-clock deadline**. See [throttle configuration](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/config/initializers/sidekiq.rb:101) and [retry policy](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/workers/tax_preparation/tax_automations/operation_worker.rb:9).

2. **Webhooks need a bounded reconciliation backstop.** Instead’s sweep runs every **30 minutes**, selecting uploaded documents still `sent` after **1 hour** or `processing` after **12 hours**, within **2 days of upload**. Older sends remain unchanged; recovery is therefore bounded. Reconciliation groups reads by entity/year, follows pagination, then individually fetches candidates absent from every folder page. An individual document 404 becomes `archived`; a missing/inaccessible folder is skipped. Both webhook and polling results use the same status mapper, which ignores duplicate states and refuses backward transitions. Reconciliation requests get one attempt per sweep; the sweep itself allows three retries. GruntWorx should inherit this recovery mechanism and explicitly choose its recovery window. See [candidate bounds](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/queries/tax_preparation/tax_automations/documents/reconcile_candidates_query.rb:8), [page continuation](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/workers/tax_preparation/tax_automations/instead/documents/reconcile_statuses_worker.rb:43), and [individual fallback](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/instead/documents/reconcile_status.rb:36).

3. **Keep a stable, shared failure vocabulary.** The document model owns eight reasons: `unexpected`, `no_active_connection`, `network_error`, `unauthorized`, `api_error`, `exceeded`, `forbidden`, and `encrypted`. Instead maps `password_required` to `encrypted`; an unknown indexing refusal still produces `error`, with no invented reason. Webhook parsing only accepts token-shaped reason strings because arbitrary vendor text could contain filenames. GruntWorx should supply its own explicit mappings and preserve the distinction between transient failures and terminal refusals. Successful recovery clears obsolete reasons. See [shared vocabulary and transitions](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/tax_preparation/tax_automations/document.rb:12), [Instead mapping](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/instead/documents/apply_processing_status.rb:10), and [reason filtering](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/forms/tax_preparation/webhooks/tax_automations/instead/event_form.rb:84).

4. **Signed-URL cassettes must control time.** Instead’s `:vcr_fixed_time` examples freeze replay at the cassette’s original recording time, keeping recorded `ExpiresAt` values meaningful; new recordings use the real clock. Client specs replay live exchanges, derive UUIDs from responses, and validate payloads against the vendor contract. Production upload transport separately checks expiry, streams multipart bytes with signed fields before the file, and sends no vendor authorization headers to the bucket. Reuse these testing and transport guarantees wherever GruntWorx uses signed uploads. See [cassette clock handling](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/spec/support/vcr_fixed_time.rb:3), [client specs](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/spec/unit/tax_preparation/lib/tax_automations/instead/client_spec.rb:5), and [upload transport](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/lib/tax_preparation/tax_automations/base_client.rb:243).

5. **Entity matching should prefer durable identity and abstain on ambiguity.** Instead reuses a stored entity across tax years, scoped by firm, client, contact, and entity type—important because entity creation is non-idempotent. Matching imported entities considers only active, unlinked records of the correct firm/type and links only a unique match. It normalizes punctuation, whitespace, case, and business legal-form spellings; personal-name swapping is a fallback. An account name represents a person only when the account has one contact. Multiple namesakes remain unlinked, with separate match metrics. Preserve those safeguards, while adapting matching keys to GruntWorx’s identity model. See [stored identity lookup](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/instead/clients/find_entity.rb:24) and [matching rules](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/instead/clients/link_entity_by_name.rb:48).

These findings come from the existing code and specs. No files were edited; tests were not run.
